title: Methyl β-Cyclodextrin-sperm-mediated gene editing for targeted mutant mouse production
author: Moradbeigi, Hosseini, et al.
materials: The present study received ethical and research committee approval from the veterinary faculty of Shiraz University (99GCB4M154630). Unless stated otherwise, all the chemicals used in this study were obtained from Sigma-Aldrich Chemical Co.

using an online gRNA design tool. To determine unique target sites in the mouse genome, the guide strands were designed to target the first exon at position 184–203 base pairs. These strands were synthesized as sense and antisense oligodeoxynucleotides with a BbsI-specific sticky end at the 5’ terminus (sense strand sequence: 5’ CACCGGCCCAGTGGATCTAAATGA 3’, and antisense strand sequence: 5’ AAACTCATTTAGATCCACTGGGCC 3’). Subsequently, the annealed complementary oligos were ligated with T4 DNA ligase into digested pgRNA-Cas9 vectors that were linearized with the BbsI enzyme. The resulting structure was then propagated in an stbl4-competent bacterial strain. To ensure correct ligation, the insert sequence was validated through colony PCR using the following primers: forward primer 5’ GATACAAGGCTGTTAGAGAG 3’ (U6-F) and reverse primer 5’ AAACTCATTTAGATCCACTGGGCC 3’ (antisense gRNA) and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The confirmed colonies were then cultivated, and plasmid DNA was extracted. The concentration and quality of the purified plasmid were evaluated using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific, USA) as well as 0.8% agarose gel electrophoresis. Finally, this plasmid was utilized for further investigations.

steps.title: Construct plasmids for CRISPR editing
steps.instruction: Generate the pCAG‑GFP and pgRNA‑Cas9 plasmids, insert the Gdf8‑targeting sgRNA, and verify plasmid quality before use.

substeps.instruction: Obtain Addgene plasmids plenti‑CAG‑gate‑FLAG‑IRES‑GFP (Addgene #107398, pCAG‑GFP) and pCAG‑eCaS9‑GFP‑U6‑gRNA (Addgene #79145, pgRNA‑Cas9).
Transform each plasmid into Stbl4‑competent E. coli, plate on LB agar containing kanamycin for pCAG‑GFP and ampicillin for pgRNA‑Cas9, and incubate overnight.
Inoculate single colonies into LB broth with the same antibiotic, grow at 37 °C with shaking.
Purify plasmid DNA with a Favorgen miniprep kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.

Design a sgRNA targeting mouse Gdf8 exon 1 (positions 184–203 bp, NC_000067.7) using an online tool; order sense oligo 5’ CACCGGCCCAGTGGATCTAAATGA 3’ and antisense oligo 5’ AAACTCATTTAGATCCACTGGGCC 3’, each bearing a 5’ BbsI sticky end.
Anneal the complementary oligos, ligate into BbsI‑digested pgRNA‑Cas9 vector with T4 DNA ligase.
Transform the ligation mix into Stbl4‑competent cells, plate on ampicillin LB agar, and incubate.
Screen colonies by PCR using forward primer 5’ GATACAAGGCTGTTAGAGAG 3’ (U6‑F) and reverse primer 5’ AAACTCATTTAGATCCACTGGGCC 3’ (antisense gRNA).
Confirm correct insert by Sanger sequencing.
Grow confirmed colonies, extract plasmid DNA, and assess concentration and purity with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer and 0.8 % agarose gel electrophoresis.
Store the validated pCAG‑GFP and pgRNA‑Cas9 plasmids for downstream experiments.

steps.title: Prepare sperm and incubation media
steps.instruction: Collect caudal epididymal sperm from male mice and suspend them in the appropriate pre‑warmed media.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize male B6D2F1 mice by cervical dislocation and dissect out the caudal epididymis and deferent ducts.
Prepare two media: (i) HTF + 0.4 % BSA; (ii) c‑TYH without MBCD. Incubate both at 37 °C, 7.5 % CO₂ for 20 min before use.
For sham and treatment groups, place dissected epididymides in c‑TYH (no MBCD); for control groups, use HTF + 0.4 % BSA.
Mechanically tease the epididymides and gently squeeze the ducts to release sperm, then add the released sperm to the corresponding medium.

steps.title: Incubate sperm with plasmids and DMSO
steps.instruction: Treat sperm with plasmid DNA (and DMSO where required) before IVF.

substeps.instruction: Incubate sperm in their respective medium at 37 °C, 7.5 % CO₂ for 30 min (all groups except the DMSO positive‑control groups).
For the DMSO/CAG‑GFP and DMSO/pgRNA‑Cas9 positive‑control groups:
a. Collect the incubated sperm into two microtubes and centrifuge (speed not specified).
b. Resuspend each pellet in HTF + 0.4 % BSA containing 3 % DMSO and either 20 ng/µl pCAG‑GFP or 20 ng/µl pgRNA‑Cas9.
c. Incubate the mixtures at 4 °C for 15 min.
d. Centrifuge again and add the final pellet to HTF‑containing IVF droplets.

steps.title: Prepare luminol stock and working solution
steps.instruction: Make a 100 mM luminol stock in DMSO and dilute to a 5 mM working solution.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 0.0089 g luminol and dissolve in 500 µl DMSO in a foil‑covered microtube (protect from light) to obtain a 100 mM stock.
Mix 20 µl of the 100 mM stock with 380 µl DMSO in a foil‑covered tube to produce a 5 mM working luminol solution.

steps.title: Measure extracellular ROS by LDCL assay
steps.instruction: Quantify ROS in sperm incubation media using a luminometer‑based chemiluminescence assay.

substeps.instruction: Collect each sperm incubation droplet, centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min, and transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Add 2.5 µl of the 5 mM working luminol solution to 100 µl of each supernatant sample.
Prepare controls in parallel:
• Blank: 100 µl PBS.
• Positive control: 100 µl PBS + 12.5 µl 30 % H₂O₂ (v/v) + 2.5 µl working luminol.
• Negative control: 100 µl PBS + 2.5 µl working luminol.
Dispense all samples (including three replicates per condition) into a 96‑well untreated black polystyrene plate.
Measure chemiluminescence with an Orion II LB 965 microplate luminometer at 37 °C, reading 1 second every minute for 15 cycles (total 900 s).
Calculate the mean RLU per second, multiply by 900 s to obtain RLU mean for each sample, and compute ROS level = RLU mean(sample) − RLU mean(negative control).

steps.title: Assess fertilization and embryo development
steps.instruction: Evaluate embryo progression and transfection efficiency after sperm‑oocyte co‑incubation.

substeps.instruction: Six hours after adding sperm to IVF droplets, wash presumptive zygotes and transfer them to mKSOMaa medium droplets for in‑vitro culture (IVC).
After 96 h of IVC, examine embryos under a stereo microscope and record the percentages of:
• Fertilization (presence of two pronuclei, 2PN),
• 2‑cell, 4‑cell, compacted morula, and blastocyst stages.
Inspect blastocysts for GFP fluorescence (CAG‑GFP, pgRNA‑Cas9, and positive‑control groups) using a fluorescence microscope and calculate the proportion of GFP‑positive blastocysts.

steps.title: Generate and analyze mutant F0 mouse
steps.instruction: Produce a targeted Gdf8 mutant mouse via SMGT and verify genome editing in multiple tissues.

substeps.instruction: Incubate sperm in c‑TYH medium supplemented with 2 mM MBCD and 20 ng/µl pgRNA‑Cas9 plasmid; use resulting day‑4 blastocysts for embryo transfer into a 0.5 dpc recipient female.
After birth, euthanize a dark‑coated F0 mouse and harvest kidney, liver, brain, and muscle tissues.
Extract genomic DNA from each tissue.

Perform conventional PCR to amplify the 250 bp fragment spanning the U6 promoter to the guide region using primers U6‑F (5’ GATACAAGGCTGTTAGAGAG 3’) and the antisense gRNA primer; run products on agarose gel to check for plasmid presence (none detected).
Amplify the 445 bp Gdf8 target fragment from each tissue, purify, and submit for Sanger sequencing.

Analyze sequencing chromatograms with ICE (Inference of CRISPR Edits) software to identify indels; note a single‑nucleotide deletion 3–4 bp upstream of the PAM in kidney, muscle, and brain, indicating mosaicism.
